speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To help me understand your condition, could you please describe the consistency of your stool and how many bowel movements you have per day? Also, have you noticed any blood or mucus in your stool, and does the discomfort improve after you have a bowel movement?

speaker: Patient
text: 31-year-old female. The patient reports experiencing chronic diarrhea on most days for the past four months. She mentions lower abdominal discomfort and cramping, which is relieved by diarrhea. The patient notes the bowel movements are urgent, occasionally accompanied by mucus discharge, and often followed by a feeling of incomplete evacuation. She went camping several months ago and recalls another member of the camping party falling ill recently.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the recent camping history and illness in your group, have you noticed any weight loss, fever, or night sweats, and do you recall consuming untreated water or undercooked food during the trip? I will also check if you have any signs of dehydration or abdominal tenderness on examination.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the camping history and your partner's illness, I suspect a parasitic infection like Giardia, but we must rule out inflammatory bowel disease. REQUEST TEST: Stool_Ova_and_Parasites, Stool_Cultures, Fecal_Calprotectin

speaker: Doctor
text: Since the infectious and inflammatory markers are normal, we should look toward functional disorders. Do you experience bloating or a change in stool form associated with meals, and have you noticed any stress or anxiety preceding these symptoms?

speaker: Doctor
text: Since infectious and inflammatory causes have been ruled out, I suspect Irritable Bowel Syndrome. Do your symptoms correlate with stress or specific foods, and have you noticed any bloating or changes in stool form related to meals?
